question: How must Newtonian gravity or electrostatics be defined on a compact N-sphere, and what becomes of the Green function and shell theorem when there is no spatial infinity?

key_findings.claim: A point-source Poisson equation on a compact sphere requires a uniform compensating background because the Laplacian has a constant zero mode.
key_findings.evidence: Integrating the Laplacian over the closed manifold gives zero, so a lone delta source is inconsistent. The Green function therefore solves for a point mass/charge plus an opposite uniform density, a mathematical necessity absent in noncompact Euclidean space.

key_findings.claim: The resulting potential and force depend only on geodesic separation and admit integral expressions for arbitrary N, with explicit low-dimensional forms.
key_findings.evidence: Rotational symmetry reduces the Laplace-Beltrami equation to a polar-angle ODE. Integrating powers of sine gives the homogeneous kernel, and adding the background term fixes a globally valid potential whose gradient is monotone between source and antipode.

key_findings.claim: The spherical shell theorem is modified: a symmetric cap or shell can be represented through an effective point contribution together with the unavoidable background, and antipodal geometry matters.
key_findings.evidence: Flux through a hyperspherical cap tracks enclosed point-plus-background charge. The discussion of far points and rings shows how the Euclidean interior-zero-field statement is recovered only as a special limiting geometry.

anchors.section: Gauss flux through a hyperspherical cap

key_findings.claim: The work is a static mathematical model of Newtonian/electrostatic fields on prescribed constant curvature, not a cosmological or relativistic gravity solution.
key_findings.evidence: No backreaction, expanding metric, relativistic constraint equation, dynamics, or observation is modeled. The conclusion instead emphasizes Green functions, the compensating density, and higher-dimensional closed forms.

method.core_idea: Solve the Laplace-Beltrami Green-function problem on a compact constant-curvature sphere after explicitly projecting out its constant zero mode.
method.mechanism: Rotational invariance reduces the PDE to an ODE in geodesic angle. A delta source is balanced by uniform opposite density, the radial equation is integrated using the N-sphere volume element, flux yields the force law, and cap/ring integrals generalize Newton's shell theorem.
assumptions: Space is a static round N-sphere with exact constant curvature and no boundary.
Gravity is described by linear Newtonian Poisson theory, or equivalently electrostatics, on that manifold.
The compensating uniform density is part of the field definition rather than independently dynamical matter.
Sources and test particles can be treated as ideal points or symmetric distributions.

techniques.role: Makes the Poisson equation solvable on a compact manifold.
Converts the N-dimensional Laplace-Beltrami equation to an angular ODE.
Relates force flux to point source plus compensating cap density.
Derives constant-curvature analogues of Euclidean shell equivalence.

evaluations.setting: General round S^N with a unit point source and uniform compensating density.
evaluations.metric: Exact satisfaction of the distributional Poisson equation and zero total source.
evaluations.result: The derived Green function is globally consistent and has the required singularity and compact-space neutrality.
evaluations.baseline: A naive lone-delta Euclidean Green function, which violates the compact integral constraint.

evaluations.setting: Hyperspherical cap and symmetric ring/shell configurations.
evaluations.metric: Flux and equality of the resulting radial force with an effective source description.
evaluations.result: The analysis yields a modified shell theorem with antipodal and background contributions explicit.

evaluations.metric: Closed-form potential expressions from the general integral.
evaluations.result: The appendix lists explicit forms and recovers the familiar logarithmic special structure in two dimensions.

limitations: Only a round constant-curvature compact manifold is considered.
Newtonian gravity on a fixed manifold omits general-relativistic backreaction and cosmological dynamics.
The compensating uniform background is mathematically required but its physical interpretation depends on the application.
No numerical, experimental, or observational test is offered.
failure_modes: Using the Euclidean point potential without removing the zero mode produces an unsolvable compact Poisson equation.
Interpreting the background as optional leads to globally inconsistent flux.
Applying the shell result to nonuniform curvature or nonsymmetric matter invalidates the one-angle reduction.
Treating the construction as relativistic cosmology overstates its physical scope.
reusable_insights: Elliptic equations on compact manifolds require compatibility with the kernel of the differential operator.
Green functions should be defined modulo/projected against zero modes before numerical discretization.
Symmetry plus flux can generalize classical force theorems without solving every source integral directly.
open_questions: How do analogous potentials and shell theorems change on compact hyperbolic quotients or other topologies?
What is the controlled Newtonian limit of relativistic perturbations on a closed cosmology?
Can the zero-mode-projected formulation improve N-body simulations on compact spatial manifolds?

competitive_landscape.title: Generalizing Shell Theorem to Constant Curvature Spaces in All Dimensions and Topologies
competitive_landscape.relationship: Directly extends shell-theorem analysis across constant-curvature geometries, dimensions, and global topologies.
competitive_landscape.difference: It broadens beyond the round compact N-sphere; the present paper provides the explicit compact-sphere Green function, compensating background, and detailed cap/ring interpretation.

competitive_landscape.title: Minimum Energy Problem on the Hypersphere
competitive_landscape.relationship: Studies Newtonian-potential interactions and equilibrium charge distributions constrained to a hypersphere under external fields.
competitive_landscape.difference: It uses the ambient Euclidean Newtonian kernel for an energy-minimization problem; this paper derives the intrinsic Laplace-Beltrami Green function on the sphere itself.

competitive_landscape.title: Grounded Hyperspheres as Squashed Wormholes
competitive_landscape.relationship: Analyzes Green functions and electrostatic analogies involving hyperspherical geometry and grounded boundary conditions.
competitive_landscape.difference: Grounding introduces a boundary/image-charge structure; this work treats a boundaryless compact sphere where neutrality is enforced by removing the constant mode.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper derives Newtonian/electrostatic Green functions and a shell theorem on an arbitrary-dimensional round sphere with the necessary compensating background.
novelty_assessment.evidence: General integral solutions, flux arguments, ring/shell analysis, and explicit N=2–10 forms provide a self-contained construction.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The value is a clear intrinsic compact-space treatment and shell-theorem interpretation; it is mathematical physics rather than a new gravity theory.
